english: Mehmet cooked the meal patiently.
tip: 'sabırla' is 'sabır' (patience) + -la: with patience, patiently. Adding -la/-le to a noun turns it into a how adverb.

english: The children cooked the meal nicely in the garden.
tip: 'güzelce' is 'güzel' + -ce: nicely. Add -ce/-ca to an adjective to make an adverb of manner, how something is done.

english: Despite this I am not losing my hope.
tip: 'rağmen' (despite) needs the noun before it in the -a/-e form, so 'bu' becomes 'buna': 'buna rağmen' = despite this.

english: When it snowed, I got in the car.
tip: 'binmek' takes the -a/-e ending for what you board: 'arabaya bindim' = I got in the car, never 'arabayı bindim'.

english: We crossed the bridge to the Asian side.
tip: 'geçerek' is 'geç' + -erek: by crossing. Add -erek/-arak to a verb to show the means, how the main action happened.

english: My sibling and I used to fight a lot when we were little.
tip: 'küçükken' is 'küçük' + -ken: when little. Attach -ken to say while or when that state held: 'küçükken' = back when we were small.

target: Bu marketten aldığım peynir çok tuzluydu.
english: The cheese I bought from this market was very salty.
tip: 'aldığım peynir' means the cheese I bought. The -dığım ending turns a verb into a that-I-did label on the noun after it.

target: Dört katlı binanın çatısından şehri izledim.
english: I watched the city from the roof of the four-story building.
tip: 'çatısından' inserts a buffer n: 'çatı' + sı + n + dan. The n slides between the -sı (its) ending and the -dan (from) ending so vowels do not clash.

target: Otobüs trenden daha yavaş ama daha ucuz.
english: The bus is slower than the train but cheaper.
tip: Comparisons put the yardstick in the -dan/-den (from) form plus 'daha': 'trenden daha yavaş' = slower than the train.

target: Kargom geldi ama evde yoktum, komşuya bırakmışlar.
english: My package arrived but I wasn't home, they left it with the neighbor.
tip: 'bırakmışlar' uses -mış for something you did not witness: apparently they left it. It reports or infers rather than states firsthand.

english: You are waiting at school right now.
tip: The -iyor ending is the present continuous for what is happening now: 'bekliyorsunuz' = you are waiting, lines up with 'şu anda' = right now.

english: Yesterday I met my old school friend.
tip: The -la ending means with and stacks after the my-ending: 'arkadaş' plus -ım (my) plus -la gives 'arkadaşımla' = with my friend.

english: I like reading books before going to sleep.
tip: To say before doing something, put -madan önce on the verb: 'uyumadan önce' = before sleeping.

english: The ferry was delayed because of the strong wind.
tip: 'yüzünden' means because of and is used for a cause you blame: 'rüzgâr yüzünden' = because of the wind, points at what caused the delay.

english: If you take this road you'll reach the highway.
tip: The -se ending means if: 'giderseniz' = if you go, setting up the condition for the rest of the sentence.

english: I need to renew my passport before the trip.
tip: To say I need to do something, use the verb plus -mem gerekiyor: 'yenilemem gerekiyor' = I need to renew.

target: Her ihtimale karşı yanımda nakit taşırım.
english: I always carry cash just in case.
tip: 'her ihtimale karşı' is a fixed phrase meaning just in case, literally against every possibility.

target: Yağmur aniden bastırınca koşarak eve gittim.
english: When the rain suddenly started I ran home.
tip: The -arak ending means by or while doing: 'koşarak' = by running, describing how I got home.

target: Marketten yumurtalar, ekmekler ve süt aldık.
english: We bought eggs, bread and milk from the market.
tip: Plurals take -lar after back vowels and -ler after front ones: 'yumurtalar' (eggs) but 'ekmekler' (breads).

target: Dondurma almak için uzun bir kuyruk vardı.
english: There was a long queue to buy ice cream.
tip: An infinitive plus 'için' means in order to: 'almak için' = in order to buy.

target: Annem her zaman şarkı söyledi ama yarıda bıraktı.
english: My mom always sang but stopped halfway.
tip: Turkish says 'şarkı söylemek', literally to say a song, for to sing: 'şarkı söyledi' = sang.

english: Hasan angrily gathered his things from the office.
tip: Add -yle to a noun to say with that feeling: 'öfke' (anger) plus -yle gives 'öfkeyle' = angrily.

english: The pharmacist nicely finished her work at the station.
tip: The -ce ending turns an adjective into an adverb: 'güzel' (nice) becomes 'güzelce' = nicely.

english: The archaeologist carelessly said the news at the office.
tip: A specific, known object takes -i: 'haber' becomes 'haberi', marking the news as a definite thing already in mind.

english: Bean pilaki is the king of olive oil dishes.
tip: Both nouns get marked in this chain: 'zeytinyağlıların' ends in -ın (of the dishes) and 'kralı' adds -ı pointing back, so 'kralıdır' = their king.

english: Cucumber is the indispensable ingredient of cacik.
tip: 'olmazsa olmazı' is a set phrase for the indispensable part, literally if-it-isn't it-isn't, so 'cacığın olmazsa olmazı' = the must-have of cacik.

english: The two teams competed with each other.
tip: 'birbiri' means each other, and with -yle it becomes 'birbirleriyle' = with one another.

english: Of the four seasons, my favorite is autumn.
tip: Put 'en' before an adjective for the superlative, the most: 'en sevdiğim' = the one I love most.

english: The guard opened the gate for the visitors.
tip: The -çi ending names the person who does something: 'bek' plus -çi gives 'bekçi' (guard), and 'ziyaret' plus -çi gives 'ziyaretçiler' = visitors.

english: We went from Istanbul to Ankara by train.
tip: -dan marks from and -ya marks to: 'İstanbul'dan' 'Ankara'ya' = from Istanbul to Ankara.
